messages:
anya: Quick thread to align on the shadow-envelope storage migration. Goal: no console regressions, safe fast rollback, and clear telemetry for routing/quotas.
rohan: Outline?
anya: Plan is dual-write -> shadow reads for verification -> staged cutover. Need concrete gates for dashboard alerts and quota routing correctness.
mike: For dual-write, stamp a small `ingest_version` field on the envelope (e.g. `v2-envelope-2024`) so reads can tell origin. Also emit a tiny reconcile key: `route_hash` to ease diffing.
jess: UX: console should show a subtle badge when results are served from shadow data and a feature-flagged toggle to flip experimental routing.ohan: Can we produce per-route delta metrics? v1_count vs v2_count per minute for each route would let us detect skew early.
eva: ingest-bot can emit that but to control cost start with 1% sampling. We should keep deterministic sampling so tiny routes still get audited.
mike: Deterministic sample idea: hash(route_id)%100 < 1 OR daily_route_count < 500. Also log full diffs for a random 50 route_ids/day for manual inspection.
anya: Good. Jess — add a dashboard card for mismatch_ratio = abs(v2_count - v1_count)/greatest(1,v1_count) and latency deltas p50/p95. That will be our primary canary signal.
jess: Will do. Also wire a support banner and make it visible to SRE/support on 20% canary.
rohan: Query perf risk: the new envelope JSON->columns projection can add CPU on hot reads. Thoughts?
mike: Mitigate by maintaining a small materialized projection table populated by the shadow-write worker. Index (route_id, day) and TTL old rows. Keep the projection compact to avoid bloat.
anya: Rollback checklist draft: 1) flip read adapter to prefer v1, 2) disable dual-write, 3) run reconciliation job and compare counts, 4) clear feature flags and notify teams. We should include exact commands in runbook.
rohan: Example commands for runbook: ```sql -- prefer old envelopes UPDATE feature_flags SET value='v1-only' WHERE key='console.ingest.read_mode'; ``` and an admin API: `POST /admin/feature-toggles/console-ingest?mode=v1-only`.
jess: Add telemetry on toggles: `telemetry("ingest_migration_toggle", {from:'v2',to:'v1',actor:current_user})`.
eva: For canary schedule propose: 5% traffic for 24h -> 20% for 48h. Abort if mismatch_ratio > 0.03 on routes with >1000 events/day or if console query p95 increases >25%.
mike: Enforce the p95 abort in rollout controller: if p95_new / p95_old > 1.25 then auto-fail. I'll add sample SQL to create the projection index in the runbook: `CREATE INDEX ix_ingest_proj_route_day ON ingestion_projection (route_id, day) WHERE day >= current_date - interval '14 days';`
rohan: Also add a safepoint snapshot step: export routing metadata used by join keys before cutover to speed reconciliation.
anya: I'm volunteering to author the runbook and coordinate with eng-sre. Jess will handle console UI, Eva telemetry/ingest-bot changes, Mike projection/index, Rohan rollout job.
ingest-bot: automated: shadow-write cron will start 2024-05-03T02:00Z if feature flags set :gear:ohan: small nit: add a step to ping #support-alerts when canary reaches 20% so support can monitor inbound tickets.
jess: added to checklist.
anya: Final note: include a short pardoned sample of the reconciliation query in the runbook to compare route counts: ```sql SELECT route_id, sum(case when ingest_version='v1' then 1 else 0 end) AS v1_count, sum(case when ingest_version='v2' then 1 else 0 end) AS v2_count FROM ingestion_events WHERE day = current_date - 1 GROUP BY route_id HAVING greatest(sum(case when ingest_version='v1' then 1 else 0 end), sum(case when ingest_version='v2' then 1 else 0 end)) > 10; ```
anya: I'll open the runbook PR now and tag owners. Planning to enable dual-write Tue AM unless objections. :eyes:
mike: I'll drop index DDL to the PR in a bit.
eva: I'll push the mismatch metric and the telemetry events, and add the sampling config.
rohan: I'll implement the p95 auto-abort and the canary gating job.
jess: Will prep the console banner and dashboard card.
anya: Thanks all. Closing thread, follow-up in PR.
